body:
## Summary

SPEC-16 adds an explicit, provider-pinned final review for complete MR/PR changes and ordered stacks. Existing incremental-push behavior remains separate.

```text
final-review <author> [provider ref or URL]
  ├─ discover and strictly validate the provider graph
  ├─ materialize immutable revisions in disposable trees
  ├─ review every individual unit and its ordered composition
  │    ├─ independent full-repository static lenses (bounded concurrency)
  │    ├─ required repository verification
  │    └─ isolated SPEC-15 provisional-coverage checks
  ├─ preserve findings independently of any inference provider
  └─ publish guarded individual and combined results
```

- Supports GitLab and GitHub, accessible foreign authors and forks, numeric IDs, and full provider URLs.
- Scopes provisional coverage to added, changed, or dependency-affected public APIs, with requested-SHA-pinned dependencies and bounded, attributed ephemeral probes.
- Uses `compute_verdict` as the sole finding-disposition authority: `pass`, `findings`, `stale`, or `incomplete`; unavailable mandatory work never becomes a reduced-scope pass.
- Requires independently verified tree findings or executed-confidence evidence for resolved/falsified findings; quiet reruns retain memory.
- Preserves conflicts and provider warning classifications. Missing required artifacts remain `incomplete`; genuinely unrunnable dynamic work has scoped warnings; reproduced failures are blocking findings.
- Uses an independent, standard-SQLite store for contracts, runs, findings, acceptance records and exports. It has no Kimchi or review-gate state/configuration coupling. Resolution is `--store` > `FINAL_REVIEW_STORE` > `~/.final-review/final-review.sqlite3`.
- Limits credential exposure, sanitizes persisted diagnostics and worker evidence, cleans disposable trees through process-group timeouts, and confines publication to the trusted orchestrator.

## Evidence

- **Before:** review-gate operated incrementally; there was no explicit complete-provider-graph review command or combined composed-tree result.
- **After:** `review-gate.py final-review`, provider adapters, stack composition, disposition guarantees, dynamic probes, portable storage, views and acceptance runners are implemented with regression tests.

Final deterministic acceptance registry: **21/21 scenarios matched the declared outcomes**, including correct adverse, stale, incomplete and scope-control outcomes. Operator and raw-SQLite reads verified independently of the coding tool.

Real-model acceptance: **3 passed with genuine evidence**, one remains **incomplete**: `spec16-06-final-only-comment-testing-standards` hit its explicit 1800-second timeout. No timeout was promoted to a pass.

Final full suite: **2,495 passed, 5 skipped, 1 failed**. The sole failure is `tests/test_parallel_chunks.py::test_a_limit_stops_the_sibling_but_finished_chunks_keep_their_records`, whose expected chunk 3 was canceled before its review call. The same assertion was reproduced on isolated unmodified base `e272566`; a separate full run passed 2,494 tests. It is retained as a pre-existing timing-related defect, not attributed to this PR.

Changed-file Ruff and baseline/working-tree whitespace checks pass. All 12 stop tests pass after the final whitespace-only fixture correction. Independent Standards/Spec/security reviews produced substantive correctness and isolation fixes; no live provider mutations were used during development.

**Pre-push disclosure:** the existing incremental pre-push inference timed out after 600 seconds (`de6178a9fa62c971`) and after a documented 1200-second retry (`ef4e27a2ae079db7`). It produced no verdict. The operator explicitly authorized `git push --no-verify` for this push; no successful pre-push review is claimed. The new explicit final-review is still to be run independently against this PR.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The new final-review interface is additive and its code can be reverted. Existing provider integrations and legacy incremental hooks remain available. Independent SQLite migrations preserve prior schemas; no external provider publication or destructive migration is needed to merge.

**Blast Radius:** broad, explicit-command scope

Adds the complete review path, provider implementations, verification and memory lifecycle, publication commands, acceptance tooling, and tests. The main runtime risks are long or externally unavailable inference/repository operations—which must yield an incomplete/error rather than an unwarranted pass—and live provider status permissions. Merging does not grant additional credentials or run provider publication by itself.
title: SPEC-16: explicit final whole-stack review
